input: # leniency.tsv - jsonic base leniency must NOT leak through the CSS plugin.
# dialect, and across the tabnas grammar plugins its base leniency leaking
# through a plugin has been a recurring source of over-acceptance. None of the
# documents below is CSS, so a CSS parser must reject every one of them.
# ts/test/leniency.test.ts additionally asserts the stronger EQUIVALENCE
# property: the documented stack and `new Tabnas().use(Css)` (no jsonic)
# NOT a probe: `a:{b:1}`. It looks like a jsonic object but it is also a
# well-formed CSS qualified rule (selector `a:`, block `{b:1}`), and this
# plugin parses it as one. A fixture demanding ERROR there would be a FALSE
# oracle, not a real conformance gap.
# The brace-first documents below (`{a:1}`, `{"a":1}`, `{}`) are where the two
# CSS authorities disagree: CSS Syntax L3 accepts them as a qualified rule with
# an EMPTY prelude, while reworkcss/css - the AST model README.md claims, and
# the bar set in AGENTS.md - throws "selector missing". This plugin follows
# reworkcss, so ERROR is the expectation here.
